title: ESP Labs: thirteen interactive microcontroller lessons

provenance.source: Reference video supplied by the channel owner (downloaded from Facebook, 1280x720).
provenance.method: 24 frames sampled evenly plus full-size stills.
provenance.audio_finding: The file has no audio stream.
provenance.what_it_is: A screen recording of a web app, not a rendered animation: a pointer clicks through thirteen lessons, about 8 s each. Each lesson has a live isometric 3D scene on the left and a control panel on the right.
provenance.reuse: A model for the later 'machines and electronics' channel, and the source of the paper-blueprint style pack.

builder_instructions: Recreate a 108 s landscape tour of an interactive lesson page on cream graph paper. A top strip lists thirteen numbered lessons with line icons; the current one is underlined in rust. Left: an isometric 3D scene of a development board on a breadboard with coloured jumper wires and the device for that lesson, animated by a running simulation. Right: a panel with a dark Pause button, four tabs, three numbered points, toggles, live value tiles and a serial monitor. A caption box at the bottom left states the lesson in one sentence. As a video, build each lesson as one beat and move a pointer between them.

intent.goal: Show that each electronics concept can be run, watched and changed, not just read about.
intent.audience: Hobbyists and students starting with microcontrollers.
intent.takeaway: Thirteen small, working circuits, each with its code and live values.
intent.hook: A tiny display, lights and radios, all running in the browser.

labels_and_values.family: monospace (IBM Plex Mono or JetBrains Mono)

style.materials: flat-shaded isometric models with thin dark outlines, no gloss; soft contact shadows on the paper
style.lighting: even, shadowless apart from contact shadows
style.background: cream paper with a fine square grid
style.motion_language: simulation-driven: LEDs glow, radio rings expand, text types on the display, values tick; interface changes are instant
style.transitions: none: the pointer clicks and the page changes

lesson_strip.item: number in a small circle, line icon, short name; current item rust with an underline

lesson_title.suffix: small code tag such as L07

caption.style: paper box with a rust left edge
caption.text: L07 · Poll status every 500 ms; reconnect when the link drops.

parts: Pause button with SPACE hint and a restart button
three numbered points with bold lead-ins

camera.moves: none; the scene can be zoomed by hand

objects.name: T-Display-S3 style board with a small colour display, BOOT button and USB-C

list: Wi-Fi access points and a router with expanding rings

objects.note: small rust tags such as 'from line 13' point from a part to the code line that drives it

science.accuracy_model: Values come from a running simulation of the sketch, so the scene, the tiles and the serial log always agree.

timeline.visual: RGB LED lights in red, green and blue; LEDC colour mixing with a slider; button presses with debounce.
Text appears on the board's display; a menu moves with two buttons.
Four access points and a router; the scan lists networks; the board joins and shows its IP address.
A laptop loads a page served by the board and switches the LED; a firmware update fills the spare slot and the board restarts.
A card is held over a blue RFID reader; a red NFC board writes a text record.
A phone writes to the board over Bluetooth LE; an amplifier board drives a round speaker.

avoid: decorative animation that the simulation does not drive
qa_checklist: Tile values, display text and serial log agree at every moment.
Each lesson is on screen long enough to read its caption.
The current lesson is marked in the strip.
